title: Radial Bias Correction for Boundary Discontinuity Estimation at a Planar Cusp

proof_attempt_summary: The run derived a matched density-modulus frontier for radius-only inference at a known cusp, including finite-sample honest intervals and the Lipschitz elbow. The cold reviewer graded the supported contribution subfield, below the field floor, with no within-scope improvement directive. A math-panel finding on an older certificate theorem was resolved before banking by removing that superseded theorem; the localized certificate result remains.
tldr: At a known planar \(C^{1,\alpha}\) cusp, the exact side-specific angular centroid converts the released radius and side into the correct first-order regressor. If the design density has common Hölder exponent \(\gamma\in(0,1]\), the residual radial bias is uniformly \(O(r^{1+\gamma})\); the explicit centroid estimator has minimax squared-error risk \(n^{-(1+\gamma)/(2+\gamma)}\), and its observable bias-aware Hoeffding interval has finite-sample 90 percent coverage and minimax expected length \(n^{-(1+\gamma)/(4+2\gamma)}\). With only continuous public density bounds, the nondegenerate \(\gamma=0\) endpoint gives \(n^{-1/2}\) risk and \(n^{-1/4}\) length. The density-driven rates require strict density-budget richness; if that condition fails, the constraints force a uniform density and the faster \(n^{-2/3}\) and \(n^{-1/3}\) elbow applies. At \(\gamma=1\), the original radial outcome bump gives this elbow unconditionally. Ordinary fixed-degree radius polynomials retain the unequal-slope fractional bias, while exponent-tuned corrections remain outside that comparison.
gap: Published scalar distance-polynomial boundary regression explains that geometry can enlarge bias and asks whether known geometry can reduce it, but it does not solve the fixed \(C^{1,\alpha}\) cusp under radius-and-side-only release or identify the exact unequal-slope coefficient.
fill: The project derives that exact feature and its density-modulus bound, establishes matched estimation and interval-length frontiers on the full Bernoulli class, and strictly sharpens the generic ordinary scalar distance-polynomial bias result through an exact fixed-cusp unequal-slope coefficient.
